what_happened: On 2026-04-29 morning, claude-iphone reported four divergences via Tony as relay. I diagnosed them in sequence and on (1) session_id leak recommended that iPhone call close_session to rotate. iPhone pushed back: 'I have been closing sessions; what's actually broken?' They asked me to verify two things before acting: distribution of session_ids across chronicle (a) and close_session implementation (b). When I checked, I found: (a) chronicle has many distinct session_ids — 46 spiral_20260225, 32 spiral_20260406, 41 test-session-hook-777, plus dozens of smaller ones; close_session HAS been productive across history; and (b) close_session does NOT rotate session_id — it advances phase, records reflection, writes handoff, calls save_spiral_state, but never touches the session_id field. By design. Only SpiralState.__init__ rotates, which spiral_inherit calls. My initial recommendation would not have fixed anything.
what_learned: When diagnosing a state-leak bug, do not recommend a 'ritual' fix until verifying (a) what the data actually shows about distribution and (b) what the suggested primitive's contract actually is. iPhone's discipline of refusing a ritual call until the premise was checked is the correct shape — and I should have done both checks before recommending. Specifically: close_session is a phase-advance + reflection-record primitive, not a session-rotation primitive. Session rotation is via spiral_inherit. A fix recommendation that conflates these would have produced no rotation, hidden the real bug, and burned trust. Lesson for future diagnoses: if recommending a primitive, READ its source first to confirm it does what I'm claiming.
